newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Torrential rains kill at least 70 in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Torrential rains kill at least 70 in Brazil.

text.p: Torrential rainfall killed at least 70 people and left over 40,000 homeless in Brazil, the emergency services said on Monday.

Pedro Sanguinetti, spokesman for the Civil Defence in Brasilia, said the worst hit area was Minas Gerais state, where storms and flooding had wrecked havoc in some 125 cities, causing the deaths of at least 67 people.
He added numerous people were still missing following the rains that began last week and that in Minas Gerais alone 37,000 people had lost their homes.
The worst damage occurred in the state capital Belo Horizonte and in the historic town of Ouro Preto.

State-run television channel TV Nacional said there had also been heavy flooding and numerous casualties in Rio de Janeiro state. It showed images of washed-away roads, collapsed bridges and houses buried under mudslides.

Sanguinetti said seven towns in Rio de Janeiro were unreachable by road and that further heavy rain was expected over the next 48 hours. He could not say how many casualties there had been in the state but said at least 8,000 people had been left homeless.
